# Task P5-08: Ecosystem compatibility — release/push, the OpenAPI UI, Homepage/Unpackerr/autobrr contract tests

**Phase:** 5 · **Depends on:** none · **Suggested tier:** T2 standard worker · **Estimated size:** M

## Goal

Tools that talk to Lidarr keep working when pointed at Wondarr (ARCHITECTURE §5.6 "Ecosystem compatibility"): Homepage's Lidarr widget shows counts, Unpackerr can poll the queue, autobrr's "push to Lidarr" action gets an answer it understands, and a human can browse the API at `/docs`. The exact calls these tools make were verified from their current source on 2026-10-07 (below); this task pins them with contract tests and fills the gaps.

### What the tools call (verified 2026-10-07, researcher agent)

- **Homepage** (`gethomepage/homepage` `src/widgets/lidarr/widget.js`, `component.jsx`): `GET /api/v1/{endpoint}?apikey={key}` (the key as a **query parameter**) for `artist` (reads `data.length` — the response must be a **bare JSON array**), `wanted/missing` (reads `totalRecords`), `queue/status` (reads `totalCount`); `calendar` is mapped but not called by the component.
- **Unpackerr** (`Unpackerr/unpackerr` `pkg/unpackerr/lidarr.go` + `golift.io/starr` `lidarr/queue.go`): `GET /api/v1/queue?page=N&pageSize=M&sortKey=timeleft&includeUnknownArtistItems=true` with `X-Api-Key`, paging until it has `totalRecords`; per record it reads `title`, `status` (`"completed"` = finished), `trackedDownloadStatus`, `protocol` (`"torrent"`/`"usenet"`), `outputPath`, `size`, `sizeleft`, `downloadId`, `artistId`, `albumId`, `statusMessages`, and the page's `totalRecords`/`records`. Unpackerr only extracts archives for `torrent`/`usenet` downloads; Wondarr's Soulseek and YouTube items must simply not confuse it.
- **autobrr** (`autobrr/autobrr` `pkg/arr/lidarr/{lidarr,types,client}.go`, `internal/action/run_lidarr.go`): `POST /api/v1/release/push` with `X-Api-Key`, body `{ title, infoUrl?, downloadUrl?, magnetUrl?, size, indexer, downloadProtocol, protocol, publishDate, downloadClientId?, downloadClient? }`; the response is **one JSON object** `{ approved, rejected, temporarilyRejected, rejections: [string] }` — autobrr treats `rejected || temporarilyRejected` as a rejection and shows `rejections`; on HTTP 400 it decodes an array of `{ propertyName, errorMessage, errorCode, attemptedValue, severity }`. Its connection test is `GET /api/v1/system/status` (200 = OK, 401 = bad credentials) reading `version`.

## Deliverables

- `src/Wondarr.Api/Release/ReleasePushController.cs` (+ resource records) — `POST /api/v1/release/push`:
  - Body as above (all optional except `title`; unknown fields ignored). Missing/blank `title` → **400 with the array shape** above (`propertyName: "Title"`, `errorMessage: "Title is required"`, `severity: "error"`), not RFC 7807 — autobrr reads that array.
  - Parse the title as a release name (`"Artist - Title"`, with an optional `[FLAC]`/`(320)`-style quality hint; reuse the existing filename/path parser in `src/Wondarr.Core/` if one fits — look for the Soulseek filename parser and the version-flag parser) and look for a **monitored wanted song** (missing or cutoff unmet) whose main artist and title match (normalised the way the engine normalises — reuse, do not reinvent).
  - Decide: until a source can take a pushed torrent/NZB (Phase 7) every push is answered `200 { approved: false, rejected: true, temporarilyRejected: false, rejections: [...] }` with the reasons: `"No wanted song matches '<title>'"` when nothing matched, and in every case `"No download client for protocol '<protocol>' (torrent and usenet sources arrive in a later release)"`. A matched song is named in the response (`songId`, `songTitle` extra fields are fine — extra fields do not break autobrr). Never grab, never enqueue, never store anything; log one Information line (title, protocol, outcome — no URLs: download URLs can carry passkeys).
  - DECISIONS build session 6 #7 is the rule.
- The OpenAPI UI at `/docs`: add the **Scalar** API reference (`Scalar.AspNetCore`, MIT; `dotnet add src/Wondarr.Api package Scalar.AspNetCore` — let NuGet pick the current version and pin what it picked in the `.csproj` as usual) mapped at `/docs` (and `/docs/` ) reading the existing document at `/docs/v1/openapi.json`, honouring the URL base (the app supports a configurable URL base — look at how the frontend and `MapOpenApi` handle it in `Program.cs`). Authorization: the UI page is served like the OpenAPI document is today (check `Program.cs`/the auth setup — if the document requires the API key or a login, the UI does too). Add a `NOTICE.md` row for Scalar (MIT) under third-party components (follow the file's existing format for dependencies, if it lists them; if NOTICE.md only lists ported code, add it to the dependency list wherever the repo keeps one — check `README`/`docs/architecture/STACK.md`). Offline: Scalar.AspNetCore serves its assets from the package (check; if it loads them from a CDN by default, configure the bundled assets).
- Lidarr-compatible queue fields — `src/Wondarr.Api/Queue/QueueResource.cs`: **add** (never rename or remove existing fields — the frontend uses them) `title` (the display name), `status` (Lidarr's lowercase status: `queued`, `downloading`, `completed` for Completed/Importing/Imported, `failed`, `warning`?, — map every `QueueItemState`, documented in a comment), `trackedDownloadStatus` (`ok`, or `warning`/`error` when the item failed), `protocol` (`"soulseek"` / `"youtube"` from the source type — Unpackerr ignores anything not torrent/usenet, which is what we want), `size` and `sizeleft` (bytes, from `SizeBytes` and `BytesTransferred`; 0 when unknown), `downloadId` (the item id as a string), `outputPath` (the completed download path when known, else null), `artistId` (the song's primary artist id), `statusMessages` (empty array). Check `GET /api/v1/queue` accepts and ignores `sortKey=timeleft` and `includeUnknownArtistItems=true` without a 400.
- Confirm (and fix only if needed) `GET /api/v1/artist` returns a bare array; `GET /api/v1/wanted/missing` has `totalRecords`; `GET /api/v1/queue/status` has `totalCount`; `GET /api/v1/system/status` has `version`; all four accept `?apikey=`.
- Tests — `tests/Wondarr.Api.Tests/Compatibility/EcosystemContractTests.cs` with one test per tool, each making **exactly the calls the tool makes** (paths, query strings, header vs `apikey` query parameter) against the test host with a few songs and queue items, and asserting **exactly the fields the tool reads** with the right JSON types: Homepage (three calls with `?apikey=`), Unpackerr (the queue page with its parameters; the record fields; a second page is empty), autobrr (status test call; a push with a matching wanted song → `rejected: true` with both reasons, `approved: false`, `temporarilyRejected: false`; a push for an unknown song → the no-match reason; a push with no title → 400 with the array shape; 401 without a key). Plus a test that `/docs` returns the UI page (200, HTML) with the key and is refused without it when the document is.
- `docs/api/openapi.json` regenerated (search the tests for `WONDARR_UPDATE_OPENAPI`; run that test once with it set to `1`, then once without).
- Docs: `docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md` §5.6 "Ecosystem compatibility" — replace the paragraph's claims with what is now tested (the three tools, the endpoints and fields, the push rule until Phase 7, `/docs`); `README.md` — a short "Works with" line if the README has a features section (check; skip otherwise).

## Constraints

- **Never grab or store anything from a push** in this phase; never log a pushed URL (passkeys).
- Additive changes only to existing resources.
- Build after adding new test files before running tests.

## Acceptance criteria (each must be demonstrated)

1. `dotnet build -warnaserror` and `dotnet test` green (the whole solution).
2. `EcosystemContractTests` pass for Homepage, Unpackerr and autobrr.
3. `/docs` serves the API reference with the existing auth rule.
4. The OpenAPI snapshot regenerated and its test green.

## Out of scope

- Grabbing pushed releases (Phase 7, with the torrent/usenet sources).
- Lidarr's `calendar` endpoint (Homepage maps it but does not call it).
- Prowlarr application sync (not possible — its app list is hard-coded).
